# Figure S1 | Replicate check

<!-- Generated by fig_s1_replicates.py from the campaign CSVs; do not edit by hand (re-run the script). -->

**Figure S1 | Replicate check: seeding is fast in both runs; the unseeded plateau did not replicate.**

**(a)** Best IRR so far against simulated trials for the two unseeded (uninformed) and the two seeded (TRY-informed) profitability campaigns. Solid: this work's campaigns (main figure). Dashed: replicates, an uninformed campaign (run 2026-09-16) with a different space-filling start-up design and a TRY-informed campaign (run 2026-09-23) seeded with 1,000 trials of seven replicate scouts (451 isobutanol-scout, 348 ethanol-scout and 201 price-weighted-yield trials). Open circles: first trial with IRR ≥ 25 %; star and diamonds: best designs (open: the replicate's), at their true positions; the replicate TRY-informed best (27.1 % at trial 824, beside this work's star) is given in the table only. Italic labels: products of the unseeded campaigns' best-so-far designs (co-producing: ≥ 5 g·L⁻¹ of each alcohol). Table: this work / replicate; its first two rows (seeded only) give the best seed and the first trial that beat it.

**(b)** The seven replicate scouts as in main panel c (the price-weighted-yield campaign, without a counterpart in this work, last): trials (dots), best visit (open), returned design (filled; argmax of its own objective). Dashed line and tint: this work's uninformed plateau (15.8 %). Table: trials above it, share of trials losing money, returned IRR.

Seeded search beat its best seed within 13 and 19 trials in both runs, and the replicate isobutanol scouts again visited designs above 15.8 % that they did not return. The unseeded plateau did not replicate: the replicate uninformed campaign co-produced from its start-up design on and passed 25 % at trial 104. With two runs this is an observation, not a test: 1 of 2 unseeded runs stayed on the ethanol-only plateau, while seeded search was fast in 2 of 2.

*Methods notes (not part of the legend).*
* Replicates: the uninformed campaign's 50-trial space-filling start-up design, shared with the seven replicate scouts, differs from this work's (51 trials, shared with the six scouts). This work's TRY-informed campaign was seeded as in the main figure (327 of the 330 scout trials at least as profitable as the starting strain plus 673 space-filling ones). The replicate's best seed was its isobutanol-yield scout's best visit, already above 25 %, so its 19 trials to 25 % are the same event as beating its best seed, not a second measure of speed; this work's seeded campaign passed 25 % at trial 18.
* (a) Best seeds 22.9 % and 25.1 %; bests 27.3 % and 27.1 % (trials 913 and 824), within the reproducibility margin of each other (ΔPI 0.0085 < 0.0105). After 25 trials the seeded campaigns stood at 26.2 % and 25.6 %; the unseeded ones at −11.2 % (a loss) and 9.6 %. All three campaigns that passed 27 % returned co-production designs: this work's TRY-informed 39.6 g·L⁻¹ isobutanol + 40.6 g·L⁻¹ ethanol; replicate TRY-informed 42.9 g·L⁻¹ + 11.3 g·L⁻¹; replicate uninformed 41.7 g·L⁻¹ + 29.2 g·L⁻¹.
* (b) The isobutanol scouts visited 92, 2 and 5 designs above 15.8 % (yield, titer, productivity; price-weighted yield 46); the ethanol scouts never did (best 15.3 %). Every replicate scout returned a design below this work's plateau (highest 15.5 %); "loss" in the returned-IRR column: the isobutanol titer and productivity scouts returned outright money-losers (no IRR) and the price-weighted-yield scout returned −6.0 %.
* This work's uninformed campaign stayed at 15.8 % (ethanol only) from trial 104 to trial 2,000. Every improvement of this work's uninformed campaign was an ethanol-only design (all 19 best-so-far steps; first positive-IRR design at trial 53, after its 51-trial space-filling start-up design). The replicate's 50-trial start-up design already held a co-production design with a positive IRR below the 15 % hurdle (trial 12: 9.6 % with 28.0 g·L⁻¹ isobutanol + 62.1 g·L⁻¹ ethanol), and every later improvement kept co-producing (all 21 steps): it passed 15.8 % at trial 64 (17.2 %; 11.8 g·L⁻¹ + 110.2 g·L⁻¹), 25 % at trial 104 (25.1 %; 30.7 g·L⁻¹ + 46.7 g·L⁻¹) and 27.3 % only at trial 1,603. In both unseeded runs every improvement kept the product class of the campaign's first positive-IRR design.
* "Trial" is the simulated index, 1-based: CSV trial_number + 1, or, for a TRY-informed campaign, trial_number minus its preload size + 1 (preloaded seeds excluded); only completed trials are used. IRRs are at default prices; a loss (IRR < 0, or no IRR for an outright money-loser) is drawn in the grey band. The replicate uninformed and scout campaigns ran before the model version was pinned; the replicate uninformed campaign's best design re-simulated to within 3 × 10⁻⁴ IRR of its recorded value.
